title: Visual Studio Code saves a document by writing a .vsctmp file and renaming it over the target

provenance.evidence: The installed 1.132.0 bundle asks for the atomic write by name. `out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js` holds `enforceAtomicWriteFile(e){return this.atomicReadWriteResources.has(e)?{postfix:".vsctmp"}:!1}` and `out/main.js` holds `this.fileService.writeFile(this.storagePath,q.fromString(e),{atomic:{postfix:".vsctmp"}})`. The postfix is what names the temporary; the rename over the target is the second half of the same option.
provenance.not_observed: The editor's document-save path could not be driven headlessly on this host, so the ORDER below is the POSIX order the option implies rather than a captured one. The cold CLI path WAS captured (`code --user-data-dir <fresh> --list-extensions`, 8 readings) and it writes `machineid` in place without a temporary, which is a different path and is not this pattern.
blind_spots: open, flush, fsync and close are not visible to any capture method available on this host

objects.role: the document, as it was before the save

folder.fidelity: a backend that does not declare ObserveDurableBoundary
folder.omission_note: A .vsctmp that lives for less than one reading is never seen. Dropping event 1 must still yield exactly one checkpoint, ending at the last surviving event.

expected.meaningful_durable_change: The document holds the edited text and no .vsctmp file exists. One durable change, not two.
expected.forbidden_note: A checkpoint at mount sequence 4 records a durable .vsctmp file alongside an unedited document: the save is invisible and a stray temporary is permanent. That is the four-durable-changes failure 01KZC2YXH6FG9C67JP9DQX7JH6 names, seen from the inside.

notes: The replacing rename at event 5 is the operation mesh-workspace-adapter/0 does not publish today: `rename` and `move_entry` both answer AlreadyExists for a bound destination (01KZHA2H9FZ52HXJNCNG097JQJ, design 01KZHK4VWAZRYZ65TM35T4DAY5). Until that lands the only expressible substitute is unlink-then-rename, which inserts one more forbidden sequence point at which the document does not exist at all.
The displaced object 1 produces no event of its own: a replacing rename is one operation on one name binding.
